- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in the 10–15 day horizon after recent spikes; apply a 2–3 day lag correction or dampen slope.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add a small upward bias to counteract.
- Forecast horizon 20+ days: model tends to underestimate; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment for longer-term drift.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce overfitting.
